Hoover Boulevard Suite 210 Tampa, Florida 33609 To the Stockholders of Odyssey Marine Exploration, Inc. and American Ocean Minerals Corporation: On behalf of the boards of directors of Odyssey Marine Exploration, Inc. (“Odyssey”) and American Ocean Minerals Corporation (“AOM”), we are pleased to provide the accompanying proxy statement/prospectus relating to the proposed merger of Odyssey and AOM. As a holder of Odyssey common stock, you are being asked to consider and vote on the proposals described in this document. As previously disclosed, on April 8, 2026, Odyssey entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger with its wholly owned subsidiary, Oceanus Merger Sub, Inc. (“Merger Sub”), and AOM (the “Merger Agreement”). Under the Merger Agreement, Merger Sub will merge with and into AOM, with AOM surviving as a direct, wholly owned subsidiary of Odyssey. At the effective time of the merger, each outstanding share of AOM common stock will be converted into shares of Odyssey common stock at a fixed exchange ratio of 4.5017 shares of Odyssey common stock for each share of AOM common stock, which exchange ratio will be proportionately adjusted to 0.1801 to give effect to the 1-for-25 reverse stock split that Odyssey intends to effect after the effectiveness of the registration statement of which this proxy statement/prospectus forms a part but before completion of the merger. On June 26, 2026, Odyssey, Merger Sub, and AOM entered into Amendment No. 1 to Agreement and Plan of Merger (the “Merger Agreement Amendment”), which, among other things, amends the Merger Agreement to modify the proposal described in this document to approve an amendment to Odyssey’s articles of incorporation to increase the number of authorized shares of Odyssey common stock. Following completion of the merger, Odyssey is expected to be renamed “American Ocean Minerals Corporation,” and the common stock of the combined company is expected to trade on Nasdaq under the symbol AOMC, aligning the company’s corporate identity with its strategic direction. This transaction represents a significant step in the evolution of both companies. By combining Odyssey and AOM, we believe we are creating a larger, better-capitalized, U.S.-aligned platform focused on advancing access to critical minerals from the seafloor—resources that are increasingly important to supply chain resilience, advanced technologies, and long-term industrial capacity. Each company brings distinct and complementary strengths: • Odyssey contributes decades of offshore operational experience, deep-ocean technology capabilities, and public company infrastructure. • AOM contributes capital, a growing portfolio of mineral interests, and a strategy focused on acquiring and advancing high-potential assets across multiple jurisdictions. Immediately prior to the effective time of the merger: • All outstanding AOM convertible debentures issued in connection with AOM’s bridge financing will automatically convert into shares of AOM common stock. • AOM is expected to complete a private investment (“PIPE”), issuing shares of AOM common stock and accompanying warrants to investors. Table of Contents • Odyssey intends to separate its Oceanica Resources Mexico (“ORM”) asset through a trust structure for the benefit of existing Odyssey stockholders, subject to the satisfaction of certain conditions and agreements with interested parties. At the effective time of the merger: • Each outstanding share of AOM common stock will be converted into Odyssey common stock based on the exchange ratio described above. • Shares issued in the PIPE will convert into Odyssey common stock, and associated warrants will be assumed and adjusted accordingly. In connection with the broader transaction structure: • Certain equity holders of CIC Limited (“CIC Limited”) and Ocean Minerals LLC (“OML”) will exchange their interests for shares of Odyssey common stock, subject to applicable agreements and Nasdaq limitations. • Odyssey will also hold options to acquire additional equity interests in CIC Limited over time based on milestone-driven valuation thresholds. Following completion of the merger: • AOM’s leadership team is expected to assume executive management roles. • The combined company’s board of directors will comprise entirely directors designated by AOM. • Existing Odyssey stockholders are expected to retain approximately 6.6% ownership of the combined company. A key component of this transaction is the capital raised in connection with the merger: • approximately $75.6 million through pre-transaction convertible financing; and • approximately $156.4 million through the PIPE. These financings are expected to provide the combined company with the resources necessary to advance exploration, environmental studies, and regulatory processes across its portfolio. The transaction also reflects a phased and capital-disciplined approach to growth: • Ownership positions are being increased to a majority interest in certain assets, such as OML. • Other interests, such as CIC Limited, are structured through staged acquisition mechanisms, including equity exchanges and milestone-based options. This approach will allow the combined company to increase ownership over time while aligning capital deployment with project progress and regulatory milestones. Odyssey’s Board of Directors believes that participation in a larger, better-capitalized platform provides a more compelling long-term opportunity than continuing as a standalone company. After careful consideration, including the review and recommendation of a committee of independent and disinterested directors, and after consultation by such committee with its financial and legal advisors, Odyssey’s Board unanimously determined that the merger and related transactions are advisable and in the best interests of Odyssey and its stockholders. Accordingly, the Board unanimously recommends that you vote: • “FOR” the Merger Share Issuance Proposal; • “FOR” the CIC and OML Share Issuance Proposal; • “FOR” the Charter Proposal; • “FOR” the Golden Parachute Compensation Proposal; Table of Contents • “FOR” the Equity Plan Proposal; and • “FOR” the Adjournment Proposal, if presented. The completion of the merger is subject to stockholder approval and other customary closing conditions. Your vote is important, regardless of the number of shares you own. We encourage you to read this proxy statement/prospectus carefully, including the sections entitled “Risk Factors” and “The Merger,” and to vote your shares as soon as possible. This transaction reflects a shared commitment to building a company with the scale, capital, and capabilities to participate meaningfully in the emerging marine critical minerals sector. We appreciate your consideration and your continued support. Sincerely, Mark D. Gordon Mark B. Justh Chief Executive Officer Chief Executive Officer Odyssey Marine Exploration, Inc. Only stockholders who hold shares of Odyssey common stock, par value $0.0001 per share (“Odyssey Common Stock”), at the close of business on [ ], 2026, the record date for the Odyssey Special Meeting, are entitled to vote at the Odyssey Special Meeting and any adjournments or postponements of the Odyssey Special Meeting. As previously disclosed, on April 8, 2026, Odyssey entered into an agreement and plan of merger (as may be amended, supplemented or otherwise modified from time to time, the “Merger Agreement”) with Oceanus Merger Sub, Inc., a Delaware corporation and wholly owned subsidiary of Odyssey (“Merger Sub”), and American Ocean Minerals Corporation, a Delaware corporation (“AOM,” and together with Odyssey and Merger Sub, the “Parties”), pursuant to which Merger Sub will merge with and into AOM, with AOM surviving the merger and becoming a direct, wholly owned subsidiary of Odyssey (the “Merger”). Subject to the terms and conditions of the Merger Agreement, at the effective time of the Merger (the “Effective Time”), each then-outstanding share of AOM common stock, par value $0.0001 per share (“AOM Common Stock”), will be converted into shares of Odyssey Common Stock, and Odyssey will be renamed “American Ocean Minerals Corporation.” Prior to the execution and delivery of the Merger Agreement, AOM entered into subscription agreements (the “Bridge Subscription Agreements”) with certain third-party investors (the “AOM Bridge Investors”) pursuant to which the AOM Bridge Investors provided aggregate financing to AOM in the amount of approximately $75.6 million through the purchase of convertible debentures of AOM (the “AOM Bridge Debentures”). The AOM Bridge Debentures will automatically convert into shares of AOM Common Stock immediately prior to the Effective Time, such that the AOM Bridge Investors will become stockholders of AOM immediately prior to the consummation of the Merger. Contemporaneously with the execution and delivery of the Merger Agreement, AOM and Odyssey entered into a securities purchase agreement (the “AOM PIPE Subscription Agreement” and, together with the Bridge Subscription Agreements, the “Subscription Agreements”) with certain third-party investors (the “AOM PIPE Investors”), pursuant to which the AOM PIPE Investors committed to provide aggregate financing in the amount of $156.4 million (the “AOM PIPE Investment”) through the subscription for and purchase of shares of AOM Common Stock, which shares will, pursuant to the AOM PIPE Subscription Agreement, be issued immediately prior to the Effective Time, such that the AOM PIPE Investors will become stockholders of AOM immediately prior to the consummation of the Merger. Contemporaneously with the execution and delivery of the Merger Agreement, and as a condition to the willingness of the parties to the Merger Agreement to enter into the Merger Agreement, Odyssey, certain holders of AOM Common Stock, and certain AOM Bridge Investors (the “Lock-Up Holders”), entered into lock-up agreements (the “Lock-Up Agreements”) pursuant to which the Lock-Up Holders have agreed to certain restrictions on the transfer of shares of Odyssey Common Stock held by or issued to them under the Merger Agreement, such restrictions to become effective at the consummation of the Merger. Table of Contents Pursuant to the terms of the Merger Agreement, Odyssey agreed to use its commercially reasonable efforts to (i) organize a new corporation (“ORM HoldCo”), (ii) contribute its interests in Oceanica Resources Mexico, S. de R.L. de C.V., a company organized in Mexico (“ORM”), to ORM HoldCo, and (iii) transfer its interests in ORM HoldCo to a newly formed liquidating trust (the “ORM Trust”), the beneficiaries of which would be the holders of Odyssey Common Stock as of a record date prior to the consummation of the Merger (collectively, the “Non-Core Asset Transactions”). The consummation of the Non-Core Asset Transactions in all material respects, including the formation of ORM HoldCo, the contribution of Odyssey’s interests in ORM to ORM HoldCo, and the transfer of Odyssey’s interests in ORM HoldCo to the ORM Trust, is a condition to AOM’s obligation to consummate the Merger, which condition may be waived by AOM in its sole discretion. In addition, the Non-Core Asset Transactions require Odyssey to obtain a commitment for the financing necessary to fund the activities of ORM HoldCo and its subsidiaries for at least eighteen (18) months following the consummation of the Merger. The Non-Core Asset Transactions are subject to certain third-party approvals, and there can be no assurance that Odyssey will be able to obtain such approvals or consummate the Non-Core Asset Transactions on acceptable terms or at all. If AOM does not waive the condition and the Non-Core Asset Transactions have not been consummated in all material respects prior to the termination of the Merger Agreement, the Merger will not be completed. The Odyssey Special Meeting is being held for the following purposes: 1. Proposal No. 1 —The Merger Share Issuance Proposal— To consider and vote upon a proposal to approve, as required by Nasdaq Listing Rules 5635(a)(1), 5635(a)(2) and 5635(b), the issuance of approximately 728,052,679 shares of Odyssey Common Stock to the AOM Stockholders pursuant to the terms of the Merger Agreement (the “Merger Shares”), as well as the issuance of 141,968,020 shares of Odyssey Common Stock upon exercise of replacement PIPE Warrants (the “Warrant Shares”). The number of Merger Shares will be proportionately adjusted to approximately 29,122,108 to give effect to the 1-for-25 reverse stock split that Odyssey intends to effect after the effectiveness of the registration statement of which this proxy statement/prospectus forms a part but before completion of the Merger (the “Reverse Stock Split”). The issuance of the Merger Shares and Warrant Shares will result in the issuance of shares representing more than 20.0% of the shares of Odyssey Common Stock outstanding immediately prior to the Merger, requiring stockholder approval under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(a)(1), and will result in a change of control of Odyssey, requiring stockholder approval under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(b). In addition, Mark B. Justh, a director of Odyssey and a director and officer of AOM, owns approximately 6.89% of AOM, and accordingly, because the issuance of shares to the AOM Stockholders will result in an increase in outstanding common shares or voting power of 5% or more, the issuance of the Merger Shares and Warrant Shares also requires stockholder approval under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(a)(2). A portion of the Merger Shares may instead be issued as shares of a new series of convertible preferred stock of Odyssey, as further described under “Proposal No. 1—The Merger Share Issuance Proposal.” We refer to this proposal as “Proposal No. 1” or the “Merger Share Issuance Proposal.” 2. Proposal No. 2—The CIC and OML Share Issuance Proposal— To consider and vote upon a proposal to approve, as required by Nasdaq Listing Rules 5635(a)(1), 5635(a)(2) and 5635(b), the issuance of approximately 134,111,851 shares of Odyssey Common Stock to (i) the CIC Stockholders pursuant to the terms of the CIC Limited Equity Exchange Agreement, the CIC Limited Option Agreement, and the CIC LLC Option Agreement and (ii) the OML Members pursuant to the terms of the OML Equity Exchange Agreement (collectively, the “Exchange Shares”), which number of Exchange Shares will be proportionately adjusted to approximately 5,364,474 to give effect to the Reverse Stock Split. The issuance of the Exchange Shares is part of a series of integrated transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement, including the issuance of the Merger Shares, which, in the aggregate, will result in the issuance of shares representing more than 20.0% of the shares of Odyssey Common Stock outstanding immediately prior to the Merger, requiring stockholder approval under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(a)(1), and will result in a change of control of Odyssey, requiring stockholder approval under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(b). In addition, Mr. Justh indirectly owns approximately 9.2% of CIC Limited, and accordingly, because the issuance of shares to the CIC Stockholders, when integrated with the issuance of the Merger Shares, the Warrant Shares and the other Exchange Shares, will result in an increase in Table of Contents outstanding common shares or voting power of 5% or more, the issuance of shares to the CIC Stockholders also requires stockholder approval under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(a)(2). We refer to this proposal as “Proposal No. 2” or the “CIC and OML Share Issuance Proposal” and, together with the Merger Share Issuance Proposal as the “Nasdaq Proposals.” 3. Proposal No. 3—The Charter Proposal — To consider and vote upon a proposal to approve an amendment to the Odyssey Charter (as defined below) to (i) increase the number of authorized shares of Odyssey Common Stock from 82,000,000 shares to 400,000,000 shares and (ii) increase the number of authorized shares of Odyssey Preferred Stock from 24,984,166 shares to 25,000,000 shares, in each case, to be effected at the consummation of the Merger. We refer to this proposal as “Proposal No. 3” or the “Charter Proposal.” 4. Proposal No. 4—The Golden Parachute Compensation Proposal— To consider and vote upon a proposal to approve, on an advisory, non-binding basis, certain compensation payments that will or may be made by Odyssey to its named executive officers in connection with the Merger. We refer to this proposal as “Proposal No. 4” or the “Golden Parachute Compensation Proposal.” 5. Proposal No. 5—The Equity Plan Proposal —To consider and vote upon a proposal to approve the 2026 Equity Incentive Plan, to be effective as of the Closing Date, subject to stockholder approval and the consummation of the Merger. We refer to this proposal as “Proposal No. 5” or the “Equity Plan Proposal.” 6. Proposal No. 6—The Adjournment Proposal— To consider and vote upon a proposal to approve the adjournment of the special meeting to a later date or dates if it is determined by Odyssey and AOM that more time is necessary to further solicit proxies necessary for the approval of one or more of the Proposals. We refer to this proposal as “Proposal No. 6” or the “Adjournment Proposal.” These items of business are described in the attached proxy statement/prospectus, which Odyssey encourages you to read in its entirety before voting. After careful consideration, and following the unanimous recommendation of the Special Transaction Committee, the Odyssey Board has unanimously determined that the form, terms and provisions of the Merger Agreement, including the Merger, are advisable and in the best interests of Odyssey and its stockholders, and unanimously recommends you vote “FOR” the Merger Share Issuance Proposal, “FOR” the CIC and OML Share Issuance Proposal, “FOR” the Charter Proposal, “FOR” the Golden Parachute Compensation Proposal, “FOR” the Equity Plan Proposal, and “FOR” the Adjournment Proposal, if presented. The CIC and OML Share Issuance Proposal, the Golden Parachute Compensation Proposal, the Equity Plan Proposal and the Adjournment Proposal are not conditioned upon the approval of any other proposal. The holders of at least a majority of the voting power of the capital stock issued and outstanding and entitled to vote at the Odyssey Special Meeting as of the Record Date, represented in person or by proxy, will constitute a quorum for the transaction of business at the Odyssey Special Meeting. Odyssey will include proxies marked as abstentions and broker non-votes to determine the number of shares present at the Odyssey Special Meeting. A: The Merger is structured as a business combination between Odyssey and AOM, pursuant to which a wholly owned subsidiary of Odyssey will merge with and into AOM, with AOM surviving as a wholly owned subsidiary of Odyssey. The transaction structure combines AOM’s deep-sea critical minerals exploration platform and financing strategy with Odyssey’s public-company status and listing on the Nasdaq to create a publicly traded combined company positioned to advance exploration, development, and commercialization of polymetallic nodule resources on the ocean floor. The overall structure includes several interrelated transactions designed to achieve the combined company’s strategic, financing, and regulatory objectives: • Bridge Financing . AOM has entered into bridge debenture agreements (the “AOM Bridge Debentures”) to fund AOM’s transaction-related, regulatory, and operating needs pending the closing of the Merger. The AOM Bridge Debentures will convert into shares of AOM Common Stock immediately before the Effective Time. • PIPE Financing . AOM has entered into the AOM PIPE Subscription Agreement with certain investors (the “AOM PIPE Investors”) pursuant to which the AOM PIPE Investors have committed to purchase shares of AOM Common Stock and AOM PIPE Warrants for aggregate gross proceeds in the amount of $156.4 million (the “AOM PIPE Investment”). The AOM PIPE Investment capitalizes the combined company at closing and supports AOM’s minimum financing and cash conditions under the Merger Agreement. • Non-Core Asset Separation . Pursuant to the Merger Agreement, Odyssey has agreed to use its commercially reasonable efforts to complete, prior to the Effective Time, the separation and distribution of its non-core Mexican phosphate assets (the “Non-Core Asset Transactions”), which, if completed, would remove such non-core assets from the combined company and preserve potential value for pre-Merger Odyssey stockholders. The consummation of the Non-Core Asset Transactions in all material respects is a condition to AOM’s obligation to consummate the Merger, which condition 1 Table of Contents may be waived by AOM in its sole discretion. The Non-Core Asset Transactions are subject to certain third-party approvals, and there can be no assurance that Odyssey will be able to obtain such approvals or consummate the Non-Core Asset Transactions on acceptable terms or at all. • CIC and OML Transactions . Rather than acquiring CIC and OML outright at the Closing, the combined company will acquire its interests in these companies on a staged basis over time, through a combination of equity exchanges, options and convertible financing arrangements. This phased structure reflects the fact that CIC and OML are not wholly owned and have multiple existing equity holders and financing counterparties whose interests must be addressed, and that the value and timing of the CIC acquisitions are tied to the achievement of specified regulatory milestones under the Cook Islands seabed minerals licensing regime. As a result, the combined company is expected to consolidate OML but to hold its interest in CIC as a minority investment at Closing, with the ability to increase that interest over time.
